cards.note: Black labels that are lower on the pole with yellow alphanumeric codes can be found in the north west of the country in and around the Nicoya Peninsula

In and around the city of Cartago, a unique blue text pole marking starting with P- can be found on many poles. It can be found within the city proper as well as in the small towns surrounding it, most notably extending north east of the city.
Many poles within the capital of San José will have vertical white tags with 4-5 digit vertical codes on them. Sometimes they will have a letter above them. They can be found in and around San José.

On the mountainous roads south of San José and Cartago, you can find these vertical white silver tags with vertical numbers. Most notably, there will always be a section in the middle of the tag with two horizontal numbers.

Tall ten digit yellow pole codes can be found throughout the country, but are most densley populated in the south of Puntarenas. Notably, if you find a leading 2, 8, or 9 digit on the four number section of the code, you'll almost certainly be in the south.
South of San José and Cartago there are small pole stickers with a few vertical numbers and a QR code on the bottom. From afar, it somewhat resembles a key, hence the name.
Within the central-north of the country within Alajuela and bleeding into Heredia you can find many poles with vertical alphanumeric codes.
These vertical yellow pole codes with metal on the top and bottom can be found on the 2 and 222 highways directly south of Cartago
